jobs.title: Environmental Specialist
jobs.description:
Environmental Specialist

Triumvirate Environmental, one of the largest environmental services firms in North America, is seeking an Environmental Specialist for our
Lab & Onsite Support Services (Lab/OSS)
team. As an Environmental Specialist, you will support our clients on-site by managing their hazardous waste programs & projects, utilizing state & federal regulations.  
Triumvirate Environmental provides leading organizations in the higher education, life sciences, healthcare, and advanced manufacturing sectors with diverse services and expertise to assist them with compliance management. At Triumvirate Environmental, we strive to WOW both our employees and our customers. Our unique culture fosters growth, development, education, and creativity.    
This position reports to the Regional Operations Manager. This role is based on site at client locations in the San Francisco Bay area
. You will report out of our
San Leandro, CA office.

We invite you to watch this video to discover more about the exciting responsibilities of an Environmental Specialist at Triumvirate Environmental.
CLICK HERE

Responsibilities:

Develop an understanding of OSHA regulations as well as Triumvirate’s Health and Safety practices 
Preparation of chemical and biological waste for shipment and disposal, including creation of all federal/state waste documents and managing the paperwork for the material. 
Safe handling of hazardous waste containers on client sites, as well as loading/unloading of waste from vehicles 
Conduct safety equipment and hazardous waste inspections. 
Occasionally perform and document Environmental Health and Safety (EHS) audits for clients. 
Deliver Exceptional Customer Service: Champion our commitment to the WOW! by providing outstanding support and innovative solutions to our clients 
Develop a high-level of state and federal regulatory expertise ensuring our client’s compliance needs are met (e.g RCRA, DOT, and OSHA) 
Conduct spill response measures, including the assessment of the spills and cleanup efforts 
Rotating on-call responsibilities as part of our Emergency Response team (optional)

Basic Requirements
:  
Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in the hazardous-waste industry, or relevant military experience 
Ability to work as a member of a team as well as individually 
Must demonstrate strong verbal and written communication abilities to effectively interact with clients, colleagues, and stakeholders, ensuring clear and professional exchanges of information 
Demonstrated ability to analyze complex issues, develop solutions, and implement strategies to achieve positive outcomes 
Skilled in building strong, positive relationships with clients and colleagues 
Ability to work overtime on a regular basis 
Must be willing to work flexible hours within the work week (Monday through Friday) 
Ability to complete a 2 to 3 year professional advancement program in hazardous waste management 
The Environmental Specialist frequently handles hazardous chemicals and biological waste and is responsible for putting on and taking off personal protective equipment. This role is considered safety-sensitive 
Must be able to report to the office within 1 hour during Emergency Response rotating shifts  

Valid US driver’s license 
Must have a reliable form of transportation 
Must be willing to consent to Motor Vehicle Record screening, criminal background check, pre-employment physical, and drug screen (inclusive of THC) 
Upon employment, you will be required to participate in a random drug screening program (inclusive of THC) as part of our company’s commitment to maintaining a safe and healthy work environment 
Must be eligible to work in the United States without future sponsorship 
Must be able to lift 60 pounds on a regular basis 

Preferred Requirements:

Prior relevant industry experience 
Prior successful experience in a customer service role 
Active HAZWOPER 24 or 40 hour certification 
Willingness to obtain Commercial Driver’s License (CDL) 

Besides Health, Dental and Vision Insurance, we contribute to a 401k, offer a generous tuition reimbursement program, TONS of safety training for some positions with opportunities for external trainings and certifications, Mentorship & Career Succession Planning, Relocation Opportunities, Auto/Home insurance discounts, pet assistance discount plans, discounted movie passes & more!    
To learn more about our business, culture, and the exciting work that we are doing in the industry, find us on LinkedIn, Instagram (@triumvirateenvironmental), or our website !   
Triumvirate Environmental is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace. As an Equal Opportunity Employer (EOE), Triumvirate does not discriminate based on race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or other legally protected status. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Individuals with Disabilities and Protected Veterans are encouraged to apply.  
If you have a disability and need accommodation during the application and hiring process, please contact us at https://www.triumvirate.com/contact or call us at 888-834-9697.  The requirements listed above are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. To view our California Privacy Notice and Policy, click here .  
Actual starting base pay may vary based on factors such as education, experience, skills, location and budget.
Pay Range: $28 USD - $28 USD

jobs.title: Risk Assessment Privacy Specialist
jobs.description:
Ironwall by Incogni
is an executive privacy and protection service built for organizations that need to protect their most exposed people. We help companies and institutions reduce security risks to executives and other high-profile individuals by continuously finding and removing their personal information from the internet.

Role Overview

The Risk Assessment Specialist is responsible for conducting comprehensive Open Source Intelligence (OSINT) research to identify, analyze, and document publicly available information that may expose individuals to privacy, security, or personal safety risks.

This role involves researching multiple online sources, identifying personal information exposures, evaluating potential risks based on established assessment criteria, and developing detailed Risk Assessment reports that provide clients with a clear understanding of their digital exposure.

Key Responsibilities

Conduct OSINT research across search engines, data broker websites, people search platforms, public records, social media platforms, and other publicly accessible online sources.
Identify and document exposed personal information.
Analyze findings to determine potential privacy, security, and physical safety risks.
Evaluate exposure levels and assign risk scores based on established methodologies and guidelines.
Create comprehensive and well structured Risk Assessment reports, ensuring accuracy, consistency, and attention to detail.
Provide relevant insights and recommendations to help individuals understand and reduce their exposure.
Verify research findings and ensure all information included in reports is properly documented and supported by reliable sources.

Required Skills 

Strong online research and information-gathering capabilities.
Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
Excellent analytical thinking and investigative research skills.
Ability to identify patterns and connections between different pieces of information.
Strong written communication skills.
Ability to interpret findings and assess potential risks.
Strong organizational and time management skills.
Ability to work independently while following established processes and guidelines.
Understanding of online privacy, digital footprints, and information security is an advantage.

What Makes Someone Successful in This Role

The successful candidate is naturally investigative and enjoys connecting information across multiple sources. They are comfortable spending time researching, validating details, and identifying potential exposure risks that others might overlook.
They understand that seemingly unrelated pieces of publicly available information can collectively create meaningful privacy and security concerns. Most importantly, they can turn their research into accurate, organized, and actionable reports that help protect individuals.

Here's the deal:

Meaningful work:
Help protect people's personal information and reduce the risks of online exposure, fraud, cybercrime, and other threats.
Growth & development:
Join a growing company where you'll gain experience in privacy operations, online research, cybersecurity, and data protection.
Team environment:
Work remotely with a collaborative team that values ownership, accountability, and supporting one another.

Compensation:
MXN $300,000 per year plus benefits.

Ready to join us?

If you're detail-oriented, reliable, fluent in English, and passionate about protecting people's privacy, we'd love to hear from you.
Location:
Mexico
Work Arrangement:
Remote
